top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a chemically simple, genuinely new idea (degrade rather than inhibit by recruiting an E3 ligase) that has been reproduced in many laboratories and already changed both laboratory practice and drug discovery. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the principle, and Handa's identification of cereblon explains how thalidomide-type drugs act, giving the glue strand delivered consequences and tying it to the same induced-proximity logic, so the three-person citation is defensible on priority and scope. P002 shares the discovery but omits Handa for Ciulli and splits off the glue strand, so it ranks second; P003 (ionizable lipid nanoparticles) is mature and consequential but its credit is more diffuse and empirical, and any award is preferred to none.
